correctness.rationale: For a primitive two-cycle the positions must be nonzero and of opposite sign: at zero the memory alone contracts, and the two displacements must cancel. With a=λ|x₁|, b=λ|x₂| and memory square roots u,w, cancellation gives a(u+ε)=b(w+ε), whereas the memory equations give (1+β)(a²u²−b²w²)=β(a⁴−b⁴). Unequal a,b give opposite signs, so the cycle is antipodal, with memory λ²r² and r=h/2−ε/λ>0. At the positive phase the Jacobian entries are −1+4(1−β)r/h, 2β/(hλ²), 2(1−β)λ²r, β in row order. Position reflection R gives the return derivative (RJ₊)². The trace and determinant of RJ₊ are t=1+β−4(1−β)r/h and β. The degree-two Schur inequalities reduce to 1−β>0 and 1+β±t>0, both strict for every supercritical gain, giving local exponential attraction at the smooth nonzero states. The two-step spectral radius equals its lower bound β precisely for |t|≤2√β. The trace decreases from 1+β to −1+3β, and 1−3β−2√β=(1−3√β)(1+√β), so the finite exit exists exactly below β=1/9 and at equality only the infinite-gain limit reaches that edge. At a finite edge the nonzero off-diagonal makes the repeated nonzero root defective, and squaring preserves the Jordan defect. Substitution verifies [3,8] in the exact example. The uploaded checker was inspected, not executed.
